reading.body:
Magic School raised $62.5 million across three Form D filings from August 2023 to January 2025, with each round larger than the last.

The progression is $1.7 million sold in August 2023, $17.9 million in May 2024, and $45.0 million in January 2025. Each filing was made within weeks of its first sale, and none was an amendment. The offering amounts sit just above the amounts sold, which means each round closed essentially at its target rather than being raised repeatedly.

What this data covers is capital raised by the issuer, not revenue, users, or spending. It says nothing about how much compute Magic School buys or where that compute runs. The product record describes a district-facing AI platform with a free tier and a $12.99 monthly consumer tier, which is a software business model, and the filings give no basis for connecting its growth to data centers or power.

The useful signal is the shape of the curve. A company selling AI tools to school districts tripled its raise twice in eighteen months, which suggests institutional buyers were committing budget to this category over that period. Whether that spending continued after January 2025 is not in the data.
